stopCapability.mechanism: A single file named STOP_CAPTURE in the working directory. Every running log_lift.py process checks for its existence before starting and on every loop iteration (log_lift.py lines 48, 71, 398-399, 451, read again this round). Creating it stops every logger sharing that directory - there is no way, in the code that is actually deployed right now, to stop one lift's logger without stopping all four.

steps: 1. Stop whatever new process is running (Agent or otherwise) for the affected lift(s), verifying the COM port is actually released, not just that a pid file changed.

2. Start the known-good release from D:\WhizdomLift-releases\capture-kg-692acd1 directly (not the deployed D:\WhizdomLift working tree, and not any branch with Deliverable B code merged into it), using its own vendor/ and the same Scheduled Task action pattern.

4. Record the gap (elapsed time with no capture) honestly rather than only reporting the time after port-release confirmation, per plan E.3's warning against reporting a partial window as the full recovery time.
